hints.title: Cycle Entry Identification Obstacle
hints.text: Checking visited nodes with extra collections consumes linear auxiliary space. When fast and slow meet inside a loop, what mathematical relationship exists between the head and the cycle entrance?

hints.title: Floyd Collision Distance Invariant
hints.text: The distance from head to cycle entrance equals the distance from the initial meeting point to cycle entrance modulo loop length.

hints.title: Phase-Two Pointer Alignment Procedure
hints.text: Advance slow by 1 step and fast by 2 steps. If fast or fast.next reaches null, no cycle exists. When they meet, reset slow to head while keeping fast at the meeting node. Advance both by 1 step until they collide; their collision point is the cycle entry.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in list (0 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Two-phase Floyd cycle detection in strictly O(1) auxiliary memory.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: A lookup table records seen node references using O(N) space, violating constant auxiliary space constraints.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Floyd Tortoise and Hare requires zero auxiliary allocations and at most 2 * N pointer advances.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Mathematical proof explaining why the distance from head to entry equals distance from meeting point to entry.
